name: Mutable PendingIntent (FLAG_MUTABLE)
attack_scenario: A malicious app obtains the mutable PendingIntent from a notification/service, fills the empty component with its own activity, and triggers a privileged action or reads the sender's data under the sender's UID.
negative_test_hint: from another app, try to fill the PendingIntent's empty component with "com.evil/.HijackActivity" and assert the overwrite fails because the PendingIntent is immutable

exemplar.compliant: val pi = PendingIntent.getBroadcast(context, 0, Intent(context, PayReceiver::class.java), PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE)
exemplar.explanation: A mutable PendingIntent lets whoever receives it fill in or overwrite unset fields of the wrapped Intent. When the base Intent is implicit or missing a component/data, a malicious app can redirect the PendingIntent to its own component while running with the sender app's identity and permissions. Google requires FLAG_IMMUTABLE unless mutation is truly needed (and the Intent is explicit). CWE-927 / Android 12 PendingIntent guidance.
